meta.beschreibung: The public REST API of myNextDays: property types, availability, rates, bookings, guests and tasks. OAuth2, OpenAPI 3.1, webhooks with signed deliveries.

hero.unterzeile: One REST API for property types, availability, rates, bookings, guests and tasks. Short-lived tokens, permissions per credential, events by webhook — and a schema that is generated from the code and therefore cannot go out of date.

schnellstart.heading: Your first call in five minutes
schnellstart.sub: Three steps. Only the first one runs through the interface — everything else is a call.

schritt1.text: Create a credential in the dashboard and decide what it may do: permissions per area and, if you want, only certain property types. A credential for the cleaning schedule needs no access to revenue.
schritt1.hinweis: The `client_secret` is shown once; only its hash is stored. A lost secret is not recovered, it is replaced.

schritt2.text: Exchange Client-ID and Client-Secret for an Access-Token. It is valid for one hour and carries exactly the permissions of the credential.
schritt2.hinweis: Keep the token in memory and only exchange a new one when it expires or a 401 comes back — not on every call. Revoking a credential in the dashboard blocks new tokens immediately.

schritt3.text: Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Every list answers in the same envelope: `data` plus `pagination`.
schritt3.hinweis: Then call `GET /v1/me` — it tells you which permissions and which property types this credential has, without you having to find out through a series of 403s.

konzepte.heading: Four things you should know first
konzepte.sub: Four decisions that determine the behaviour of the API. They depart from common assumptions.

objekt.titel: A property is a unit type
objekt.text: A `property` is exactly one type: a room type in a hotel, or a holiday rental. Its units (`units`) hang below it — normally exactly one, with five identical studios exactly five. The unit is what is sold, the type is what is managed and priced.
objekt.folge: Availability is therefore a NUMBER (`units_available`), not a yes/no. A hotel with 8 twin and 4 double rooms has two property types with 8 and 4 units — not one property with 12 rooms.

waehrung.text: There is no default value. Every property has a currency, and every amount in a response names it.
waehrung.folge: If the currency is missing on a property type, that is a data error and the call fails with 422 — no “EUR” is substituted. When booking, your currency must match the currency of the property type.

zeit.text: `booked_at` is the moment the guest booked — from the portal’s source, `null` if the portal does not deliver it. `received_at` is the arrival in this system.
zeit.folge: Sort “newest first” by `booked_at`, not by `received_at`: in a bulk import dozens of bookings carry the same second. Timestamps are UTC, date fields are calendar days in the time zone of the property type.

kanaele.text: There is no global “published”. A property type is visible on the marketplace, on your own website, through the portals — each one switchable on its own.
kanaele.folge: A property type is sellable only when three things come together: `status = active`, the channel is on, and there are free units. A stop sell, by contrast, applies across ALL channels.

konventionen.heading: Paging, errors, limits, idempotency
konventionen.sub: The four points that are different in every API — here with numbers instead of prose.

blaettern.text: Every list answers with `data` and `pagination`. Paging runs through a **cursor**: you send the `id` of the last item on the previous page as `starting_after`. If `next_starting_after` is missing from the response, the run is finished.

felder.starting_after: The `id` of the last item on the previous page. The recommended way — stable, even when the list changes between two pages. An unknown or deleted `id` gives 422, not an empty page.
felder.next_starting_after: Is in `pagination` as long as there is more to come: the value for your next `starting_after`. If it is missing, you are at the end.
felder.limit: Rows per page. Default 50, maximum 200 — a larger value gives 422, not a shortened page.
felder.offset: Rows to skip — for a one-off look at a particular page. Together with `starting_after` it gives 422: two position statements in one request have no contradiction-free meaning.
felder.include_total: `true` additionally returns `total`. Only ask for it when you display the number.
felder.has_more: Is in every response and says whether a further page exists — no guessing, no extra round trip.

blaettern.warumCursor: Why not simply `offset`: it describes a POSITION in the list. If a booking is added between page 1 and page 2, everything shifts by one place — `offset=50` then skips a row, and on a deletion one row comes twice. Afterwards a booking is missing from your database, and nothing in the response reveals it. The cursor names the last record you have seen and therefore cannot slip.

fehler.text: Every error comes as `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code`, a `request_id` and — where it helps — the fields that explain the error. Branch on `code`, not on the text: the text may change, the code may not.

codes.nichtAuthentifiziert: Token is missing, has expired or is invalid.
codes.ungueltigeZugangsdaten: Client-ID or Client-Secret wrong, or the credential has been revoked.
codes.scopeFehlt: Token valid, but this credential does not have the required permission. The missing scope is named in the error.
codes.objektNichtErlaubt: The credential is restricted to certain property types; this one is not among them.
codes.nichtGefunden: Not present or assigned to a different business — both cases answer the same.
codes.zeitraumNichtVerfuegbar: Booked, blocked or withdrawn from sale. No half booking was created.
codes.idempotenzInArbeit: A call with this Idempotency-Key is still running. Wait a moment, then retry.
codes.aboBestehtBereits: There is already an active webhook subscription of this credential for this address.
codes.waehrungFehlt: No currency is assigned to the property type, rate plan or booking — a data error.
codes.ungueltigeAnfrage: Formally in order, but not fulfillable in substance. The reason is in `detail`.
codes.validierungFehlgeschlagen: The request does not match the schema. `felder` names which field.
codes.zuVieleAnfragen: Rate limit reached. `Retry-After` says when it continues.
codes.nichtKonfiguriert: The service cannot handle the request safely. No carrying on without checking.

limits.text: The limit applies per CREDENTIAL, not per IP address: an agency that looks after twenty businesses sits behind one IP and should not throttle itself. Three separate buckets, so that a calendar sync does not block price setting.

eimer.token: Token exchange. Strict, because credentials are checked here.
eimer.write: Writing calls — they intervene in the sale.
eimer.read: Reading calls: the everyday work of an integration.

limits.header: Every response carries the current state with it, the successful one too — so that you can adjust your pace before you run into the 429:

idempotenz.text: When creating a booking the `Idempotency-Key` header is mandatory. Choose a unique value per operation (a UUID, for example) and repeat it when you send the same call again. Without this protection a network failure with a retry creates two bookings — and the second one blocks nights that nobody ordered.

faelle.wiederholung: Same key, same payload → the first response comes back word for word, with the header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
faelle.abweichend: Same key, DIFFERENT payload → 422. A new operation needs a new key.
faelle.laufend: Same key, first call still running → 409. Wait a moment, then retry; do not follow up with a new key.

webhooks.heading: Events instead of polling
webhooks.sub: One subscription per address, signed deliveries, retries with a growing interval. Events arise on EVERY change — even when it comes through a portal or the dashboard and not through this API.

ereignisse.reservationCreated: A booking has come into being — through whatever channel.
ereignisse.reservationCancelled: A booking was cancelled. Its own event, because it calls for a different reaction than a change.
ereignisse.availabilityChanged: The calendar of a property type has changed (booking, block, release).
ereignisse.rateChanged: A daily rate or a stay rule has changed.
ereignisse.taskCreated: A task has come into being.

anlegen.text: An `https` address and the events you want. Optionally only for certain property types. Internal addresses are rejected — the check runs when creating AND before every single delivery.
anlegen.secret: The response contains the signing secret exactly once. Save it now — it is never delivered again.

nutzlast.text: Kept narrow: IDs and the fields that describe the change. You fetch the full record through the API when you need it — that way a recipient is not sent anything that it may no longer be allowed to see.

signatur.text: Every delivery carries a header with a timestamp and HMAC-SHA256 over `ZEITSTEMPEL.BODY`, computed with the secret of your subscription. Because the timestamp is signed along with it, you can recognise a delivery that was recorded and replayed later — with a signature over the body alone that is not possible.

schritte.roh: Take the RAW body of the request, not the parsed and re-serialised object — a different byte sequence gives a different signature. That is the most common reason for “signature does not match”.
schritte.alter: Check the age via the timestamp; five minutes of tolerance is a good value.
schritte.vergleich: Compare in constant time (`timingSafeEqual`, `hmac.compare_digest`). A plain `==` makes the signature guessable.

wiederholung.text: If your address does not answer with 2xx, delivery is repeated up to ten times — with a growing interval from one minute up to one hour. Answer quickly and process afterwards; a slow recipient is counted as an error.

reihenfolge.text: Not guaranteed. Use the `created_at` of the event so as not to write an older delivery over a newer one.

doppelt.text: Is unlikely, but possible — treat the event `id` as a key and process each one only once. This promise holds for every webhook provider, not only for this one.

nachholen.text: If your servers were down, you catch up on the missed events via `GET /v1/events?since=…` — oldest first, with the same `id`s as in the delivery, at most 30 days back. A push alone is no delivery guarantee: eventually the retries run out, and without this step you are missing exactly the events you never found out about.

grenzen.heading: Limitations
grenzen.sub: Two operations are not possible through this API. Both follow from the data model. Cancelling, rescheduling and price calculation are possible.

gaeste.text: Guest data comes into being when the guest enters it or through the portal. A write path here would be a third source for the same person.
gaeste.ausweg: Send guest data along when creating a booking — existing guests are recognised by their email address. Contact fields of an existing booking can be maintained through `PATCH /v1/reservations/'{'id}`.

nachrichten.text: Reading messages and writing into an existing conversation is possible (`/v1/reservations/'{'id}/messages`). Creating a new conversation is not: a message thread always belongs to a marketplace guest account, and a business API credential is not such an account.
nachrichten.ausweg: The conversation comes into being with the guest’s first message or via the dashboard; after that the API can write in it.

finanzen.text: Payments and scheduled payment requests can be read (`/v1/reservations/'{'id}/payments`), as can the payment schedule and the cancellation scale (`/v1/properties/'{'id}/booking-conditions`). Collection runs through the guest’s booking flow with payment intents, not through a link you send out.
finanzen.ausweg: Payment requests are created in the dashboard; the API reads their status and the events belonging to them.

versionen.text: An API is a promise. These four points hold for v1:

zusagen.pfad: The version is in the path. A breaking change gets `/v2`; `/v1` keeps running alongside it.
zusagen.additiv: Within v1 only fields are added. Existing fields are not renamed and do not change their meaning.

zusagen.changelog: Changes are in the OpenAPI file and on this page. There is no silent change to a field.

zugang.heading: Authentication
zugang.sub: OAuth 2.0 with `client_credentials`. A credential belongs to exactly one business; there is no key that spans several businesses.

ablauf.text: `client_credentials` is the flow for programs acting on their own behalf. There is no consent dialog and no refresh token.

schritte.anlegen: Create the credential in the dashboard: Account → API access. The `client_secret` is shown once and cannot be retrieved afterwards.
schritte.tauschen: `POST /v1/oauth/token` with `client_id` and `client_secret`. The response contains `access_token`, `expires_in` (3600) and the granted scopes.
schritte.senden: Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN` with every call. After expiry the API responds with 401 and the code `token_expired`.

ablauf.merksatz: Keep the token in memory instead of fetching a new one per call. One exchange per request runs into the rate limit of the token endpoint (10/minute).

rechte.text: Scopes have the form `bereich:richtung`, for example `reservations:read` or `rates:write`. If a scope is missing, the endpoint responds with 403 and the code `insufficient_scope`.
rechte.merksatz: Grant only the scopes the integration needs. A lost key then cannot overwrite anything it was never meant to read.

objekte.text: A credential can be restricted to specific properties. It sees only those in lists; a call with a different property ID responds with 403 and the code `objekt_nicht_erlaubt`.

selbstauskunft.text: `GET /v1/me` returns the business, scopes and property restriction of the token — the first call when setting up an integration.

fehler.heading: What errors look like
fehler.sub: Every error is an HTTP status code plus a body per RFC 9457 (`application/problem+json`). No error arrives with status 200.

aufbau.text: `code` is the stable, machine-readable name of the error. `detail` is text for humans and can change at any time.

felder.type: Address of the description of this error type — the list of error codes in the appendix.
felder.title: Short name of the error type.
felder.code: Stable name of the error. Evaluate this field.
felder.request_id: Identifier of the request. Include it in a support request.

aufbau.merksatz: Branch on `code`, not on `detail`. The text is not an interface.

klassen.vier: 4xx — the request is the problem: missing scope, unknown ID, invalid value, occupied period. Retrying changes nothing.
klassen.fuenf: 5xx — server-side error. Retry with increasing intervals.
klassen.neun: 429 — rate limit reached. `Retry-After` gives the wait time in seconds.

limits.heading: How many calls are allowed
limits.sub: Limits apply per credential, not per IP. There are three buckets with separate values for reading, writing and token issuance.

fehlercodes.heading: Error codes
fehlercodes.sub: All `code` values of this API. Every row has an anchor; the `type` address of an error response points to it.

lokalisierung.heading: Localization
lokalisierung.sub: Language and currency come from the data. Both fields can be empty; neither has a default value.

waehrung.text: Every amount carries a `currency` code per ISO 4217. There is no default value and no conversion.
waehrung.merksatz: When creating a booking, `currency` must match the currency of the property. On deviation: 422 with the code `currency_mismatch`.

sprache.text: `language` is a two-letter code per ISO 639-1, for example `de`, `da`, `en`. The value comes from the booking or from the portal and can be empty. Empty means unknown.

texte.text: Field names, `code` values and enum values are English and part of the contract. The `detail` texts of an error response are aimed at humans and can change — show your own messages based on `code`.

zeit.heading: Time zones
zeit.sub: This API uses two kinds of time values: calendar days in the time zone of the property and timestamps in UTC.

tage.text: `check_in`, `check_out`, `date`, `from` and `to` are calendar days in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`, meant in the time zone of the property. They carry no time of day and are not converted to UTC.
tage.merksatz: `check_out` is the day of departure; the last occupied night is the night before. Four nights mean four days between `check_in` and `check_out`.

zeitpunkte.text: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `received_at`, `booked_at` and `cancelled_at` are timestamps per ISO 8601 in UTC with `Z` at the end.

quelle.text: `booked_at` is the moment the guest booked, for portal bookings taken from the portal’s source. `received_at` is the arrival in this system. In a bulk fetch many bookings carry the same `received_at` second.
quelle.merksatz: For “newest first” use `booked_at` and treat `null` as unknown. `received_at` reflects the order of the fetch, not that of the bookings.

filter.text: `updated_since` takes a timestamp and returns what has changed since then. Careful with URL encoding: `+` means a space in an address — write `Z` or encode it as `%2B`.

zielgruppen.abschluss: Whatever the shape — it is all managed in the same system, with the same login.

hotel.text: Small hotels run their rooms as room types: every type carries its units, and the occupancy plan lists each room on its own — with arrival, departure and housekeeping. Booking.com, Expedia and the other booking portals receive the number of free units, not a yes/no. Prices, minimum stay and blocks are maintained once, and the channel manager distributes them to every connected portal. Invoice, payment and guest messaging live in the same system.
hotel.beleg: Availability as a number, not yes/no.

bnb.text: Breakfast, towels, pet fee, late arrival: extras stay attached to the booking and appear on the guest's invoice without a side calculation. If you run the B&B yourself, you don't want a second list — enquiries, messages, payments and availability come together in one place, on the desktop and on your phone. Card payments via Stripe are included, as is your own booking page without portal commission.

gaestehaus.unterzeile: Management for guest houses with several rooms
gaestehaus.text: Several units under one roof, one calendar: which guest gets which room stays your decision until arrival, without recreating the booking. The building decides what the portals see under one identifier; amenities, photos and prices are maintained per room type. Housekeeping tasks follow arrivals and departures and land on the team's phone — with their own login that shows tasks, not revenue.

motel.unterzeile: Software for motels and short stays
motel.text: High turnover, short stays, late arrivals: arrival details, access codes and the invoice reach the guest automatically — at the right moment and in their language, with 24 languages ready. Rooms that free up go back to every portal without a keystroke, and a stop-sell closes them everywhere at once. At the front desk the day plan is enough: who arrives, who leaves, what is still open.

lodge.unterzeile: Rent out a lodge, from your phone too
lodge.text: Remote does not mean cut off: prices, minimum stay, changeover days and blocks are managed on your phone exactly as at the desk — same calendar, same booking, no intermediate state. Seasonal rates are set in the rate grid for a whole year instead of typed day by day, and length-of-stay discounts reach the portals as well. Even without a reception, the guest knows how to get in.
lodge.beleg: On the road too, in the app.

ferienwohnung.text: One apartment, every channel: Booking.com, Airbnb, Vrbo, our own myBestDays marketplace and direct bookings on your website share a single calendar. Once a night is sold it is gone everywhere — double bookings cannot happen. Low-commission direct bookings can be favoured on purpose: your own pricing strategy, discounts for longer stays, automated messages from booking to departure, and card payments straight to your account.

resort.unterzeile: Manage a resort with many units
resort.text: Studios, suites and villas run as their own types with their own prices, amenities and occupancy rules — all under one account and one invoice. As many properties and as many units per type as you need, without anyone switching logins. Front desk, housekeeping and owners each see only their part; owner statements are produced per property including a report, instead of a spreadsheet at month's end.
resort.beleg: As many properties per account as you need.

huette.text: Seasonal operation without handwork: closed periods, changeover days, minimum and maximum stays are set once and apply on every portal at the same time. If the cabin is closed in winter, it is closed everywhere — no logging into five extranets. The changeover day stays free between two bookings so housekeeping has time, and arrival or departure days can be blocked individually.
huette.beleg: One block applies on every portal.

pension.unterzeile: Guesthouse administration with invoices and tourist tax
pension.text: Half board, tourist tax, regulars, payment on site: the system calculates surcharges and levies correctly for each portal — including where the portal reports a net amount and you need the gross price. Invoices, credit notes and open items sit in the same record as the booking, in your country's currency. Returning guests are recognised by their history instead of a search through old emails.

campingplatz.text: Pitches, rental caravans and glamping tents are types with a count: twenty identical pitches are one type with twenty units, not twenty calendars. Availability goes to the portals as a number so you never sell more than you have. Electricity, tourist tax or a dog are charged per night or per stay, and the day's arrivals are bundled in the day plan.
campingplatz.beleg: A count instead of twenty calendars.

faq.heading: The questions that come before switching systems.
faq.sub: What the platform does, what it costs and how your data is protected — without marketing speak.

was.antwort: myNextDays is a property management system and a channel manager in one — for hotels, guesthouses, holiday apartments, campsites and agencies. Calendar, reservations, prices, portals, direct bookings, guest messaging, housekeeping and billing sit in one interface with one login, instead of four tools that know nothing about each other.

portale.frage: Which booking portals can I connect?
portale.antwort: You reach 56 booking platforms, among them Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia, Vrbo, Google, Agoda and Tripadvisor. On top of that come our own myBestDays marketplace, a booking widget for your website and regional channels. Every channel is switched separately: you decide per property where it is visible.

sync.frage: How fast does it sync — and can double bookings happen?
sync.antwort: The sync runs both ways in real time: a booking on one portal blocks that night everywhere else, and changed prices or minimum stays go out immediately. All channels share one calendar, so no second truth appears. A stop-sell closes availability everywhere at once, not only where you set it.

betriebsarten.frage: Does it fit a hotel and holiday apartments at the same time?
betriebsarten.antwort: Yes, it is the same model: every property is exactly one type — a room type in a hotel or a holiday rental — and its units sit underneath. A hotel with eight double and four single rooms has two properties with eight and four units. The portals receive the number of free units, so five identical studios don't need five calendars.

direkt.frage: Do I get my own booking page without portal commission?
direkt.antwort: Yes. Each account includes its own booking portal, a widget for the existing website, and a website builder with its own domain. Bookings made through these are commission-free, use the same calendar and prices — and the money goes directly to your account.

marktplatz.antwort: myBestDays is our own marketplace for guests — a booking channel on equal footing with Booking.com and Airbnb, only at a much lower commission. Your properties appear automatically in the marketplace and in the myBestDays guest app.

zahlungen.frage: How do payments, deposits and invoices work?
zahlungen.antwort: Online payments run through Stripe into your own account: deposit, balance or security deposit, by card and the payment methods Stripe offers in the guest's country. Invoices and credit notes come out of the booking, in the property's currency, with accounting-ready exports. Portal fees and levies are calculated correctly per portal — even where a portal only reports a net amount.

laender.frage: Which countries, currencies and languages does the platform cover?
laender.antwort: At launch on 1 September 2026 in 27 European countries. Interface and guest communication come in 24 languages; the guest reads the confirmation in their own language. Currency belongs to the property or the business — there is no euro assumption, kroner, złoty or forint are handled the same way.

rollen.frage: Who sees which data — owners, housekeeping, guests?
rollen.antwort: Every role has its own login and sees only its part. Owners see their properties, their occupancy and payouts, but nobody else's. Housekeeping sees tasks with photo checklists, not revenue. Guests have their own area with check-in, the digital guest guide and messages.

app.antwort: Two, because guests and operators need different things: the myNextDays app for the business, owners and housekeeping — calendar, bookings and tasks on the road — and the myBestDays app for guests with search, booking, check-in and messages. Both talk to the same system; nothing runs on a second copy.

sicherheit.frage: What about data protection and security?
sicherheit.antwort: Built in Denmark, hosted in the EU, GDPR-compliant including a data processing agreement. Each business's data is separated at database level, not just in the interface. Two-factor sign-in is available, role permissions limit access to financial and guest data, and every sign-in is traceable in the device history.

preis.frage: What does myNextDays cost and how do I start?
preis.antwort: 14 days free, no minimum term, no setup fee, cancel any time. After that a subscription plus a small commission on bookings we bring in. Add-on modules such as extended accounting with DATEV export, staff management or hotel functions are only added if you need them. Create a property, connect your channels, go.

laufzeit.antwort: No. The subscription is monthly and can be cancelled with four weeks' notice to the end of the month. The first 14 days are free: you enter your payment details at the start, but payment will only be charged after the trial period. If you sign up via a partner's link or code, the first full month is also free. If you cancel beforehand, you pay nothing.

objektzahl.frage: What happens when I add properties?
objektzahl.antwort: You pay for the number of properties you booked. When one is added, the extra amount is charged pro rata and is usable immediately; the next tier applies automatically once you reach it.

waehrung.antwort: We bill in euros as the anchor currency; if you pay in another currency, checkout converts at the current rate. Your guests pay in your property's currency regardless.

steuern.frage: Are prices with or without tax?
steuern.antwort: All amounts shown are net. VAT depends on your country; with a valid VAT ID inside the EU we bill without tax (reverse charge).

umzug.frage: Can I bring my data with me?
umzug.antwort: Yes. Properties, rates and bookings can be imported, and the channels are reconnected. Our team helps with the setup — at no extra cost.

kuendigung.antwort: Your properties stay bookable until the end of the paid period. After that you still reach your data and can export it; nothing is deleted until you ask for it.

hero.headlinePre: We rent out ourselves. That is why there is
hero.sub: myNextDays ApS is an owner-run company from Bindslev in northern Jutland. We rent out our own holiday properties — and built the platform we were missing every day: calendar, channels, guests, payments and accounting in one place.

warum.heading: Born out of running our own rentals.
warum.p1: Anyone who rents out knows the evening when the same week has been sold twice because one channel never received the block. That is where we stopped looking for a tool and started building one.
warum.p2: The existing systems were either made for hotel chains — with a complexity and a price no business with a handful of properties can carry — or they stopped exactly where the real work begins: accounting, owners, cleaning and taxes across 27 countries.
warum.p3: myNextDays is the answer to that: a complete property management system with a channel manager, for businesses that run their properties themselves — from a single holiday home to a hotel with several room types.

General, commercial and editorial matters go to {info}; technical enquiries, API questions and security reports to {technik}. schritte.heading: Three steps to your first commission

bewerben.text: You tell us your channel — website, social profile, or network. We review each application personally and usually approve it within a few business days.

teilen.text: You receive a personal link and a referral code. The code is visibly displayed in the registration form — without a tracking cookie.

verdienen.text: If a referred business pays its first subscription invoice, your commission runs for twelve months. You see each customer pseudonymously in the partner dashboard and are paid monthly.

bedingungen.heading: Fair for you, fair for the businesses

basis.text: Commission basis is the net subscription revenue (basic tariff and modules) of the referred business — excluding taxes, portal commissions, and additional services.

dauer.text: The commission runs for twelve months from the business's first paid subscription invoice; your customers' free month does not count. If the business cancels, it ends with its last payment. Super commission and booking share run without this limit, but require the Elite Partner rank.

auszahlung.text: Monthly, 30 days after the business's payment, from a minimum amount per currency. You receive a credit note; companies need a valid VAT ID.

kennzeichnung.text: Every recommendation is advertising and must be labeled as such. We provide the required wording for each language in the dashboard.

verboten.text: Self-promotion, advertising on our brand names in search ads, promises of discounts in our name, and unsolicited messages. Refunds will be deducted from the commission.

daten.text: You only see your customers pseudonymously — with country, status, and amounts, never with names or email. A business may allow you to contact them upon registration.

wer.antwort: Any person or company in the EU with a genuine channel to landlords or hotels: influencers, consultants, agencies, tax firms, associations — and myNextDays customers themselves. An application is free; a subscription is not a prerequisite.

wann.frage: When does a business count as my customer?
wann.antwort: When they register with your code and have paid their first subscription invoice. Registrations without payment do not count for ranking.

doppelt.frage: What if a business names two partners?
doppelt.antwort: A business is assigned to exactly one partner — the one whose code was in the form during registration. Subsequent codes do not change this.

steuern.antwort: We issue a credit note (self-billing). Companies with an EU VAT ID receive it with a reverse-charge note, private individuals without VAT — you are responsible for taxing the commission yourself.

material.antwort: Yes: short videos for social media, an explainer video, banners, and text modules — in the partner dashboard, in your language.

wieviel.frage: How much commission can I earn?
wieviel.antwort: This depends on your customers' subscription revenue and your rank. The tier above shows the rate per rank; for twelve months per customer. In addition, there is a one-time promotion bonus for each rank achieved and, with a team, the difference commission. From Elite Partner onwards, a 2.5 % super commission on your entire structure and 0.5% of each booking your customers receive via myBestDays are added — both without a time limit.

team.frage: How does the team commission work?
team.antwort: From the Climber rank: If a partner applies via your team link and visibly enters your code in the application, they become part of your team after approval. Their customers count 1:1 for your rank. On the net subscription revenue of their customers, you receive the difference between your rate and theirs — exactly one level deep, without a participation fee, without money for recruitment.

auszahlung.frage: How and when are commissions paid out?
auszahlung.antwort: Monthly per currency, as soon as the sum reaches the minimum amount for your currency. Each commission line is "open" for 30 days (refund window) and then payable. You receive a credit (self-billing) — you do not issue an invoice. Payment via SEPA, Wise or PayPal.

verfolgen.frage: How can I track my commissions and performance?
verfolgen.antwort: In the partner dashboard, under "Commissions" you see every paid subscription invoice with basis, rate, amount and status, under "Customers" your businesses pseudonymously, under "Team" the evaluation of your team partners and under "Links & Material" clicks per code.

werbung.antwort: Not on our brand: Ads on "myNextDays" and spelling variations (brand bidding), cookie dropping, purchased reach or incentives for registrations are prohibited and will lead to a ban. Your own content, contributions and recommendations are expressly welcome — with labeling as advertising.
